slot: Your question, plus the daily report
summary: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 0.25 percentage points today, the first hike since July 2023, and signaled another increase is likely before year end. That spooked stocks: the S&P 500 fell 0.45% to 7,551.81 and the Dow dropped 1.21%, while the 10 year Treasury yield, which is the interest rate the US government pays to borrow for a decade, climbed to 5.01%. Tech held up better than the rest of the market. Retail sales came in at plus 1.2% for August according to press coverage, well above the 0.8% forecast, which is good for the economy but gives the Fed more reason to keep rates higher. COST reports earnings September 24, MU on September 30.
